proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing disputes and auto-fix wrong bills, framing the August dispute surge as a response-handling problem (CL-01). Investigation defined the problem differently: dispute tickets roughly doubled from 590 (Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug 2026) and stayed elevated at 1260 (Sep 2026) (E-03), driven predominantly by billing errors on bills with ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads — 59% of the 3025 disputed bills (E-02) — a pattern consistent with an August billing import validation rule change (H-RULE-CHANGE-AUG, supported by E-02, E-03, E-12), not by slow ticket response (E-05 shows response well within SLA) or primarily by field-read estimate substitution (E-01). The release delivers only the read-only investigation scope that was completed (investigate_field_read_handoff:H-FIELD-BILL, investigate_ami_export_access:DA-MDMS) under decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION; it does not touch customer bills (K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes) or push route changes (K-DISPATCH requires Field Operations Manager confirmation, E-08). The core confirmation step — directly checking the billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) to validate H-RULE-CHANGE-AUG — remains open as VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION and was deferred, so the release does not yet confirm or fix the suspected root cause.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): dispute surge (E-03: 590→1180→1260) is predominantly on ACTUAL-read bills (E-02: 59%), pointing to a billing import validation rule change rather than response speed or estimate substitution.
The requester's framing (CL-01: an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes billing errors) was tested as hypothesis H-AI-AGENT-FIXES-WRONG-BILLS and rejected, contradicted by E-01 and E-05.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE and H-COMMUNICATION-GAP were also rejected (contradicted by E-02/E-12 and E-02 respectively); H-RULE-CHANGE-AUG is SUPPORTED by E-02, E-03, E-12; H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE and H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE remain CANDIDATE, not confirmed.

Evidence E-12 shows that for disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 of 1240 AMI reads were valid and received but rejected at billing import for high consumption, pointing at the billing import step rather than AMI export failure.
Released scope is limited to the two completed, read-only investigation items (H-FIELD-BILL, DA-MDMS); no bill writes or route-dispatch pushes occurred, consistent with K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE Gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS and the critical verification obligation VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION (confirming the rule change via DA-RULES) is still OPEN and its blocking scope sits outside this release.
limitations_explained: DA-RULES (the billing-config rule-change log) was not queried in this release; the core confirmation of H-RULE-CHANGE-AUG, the leading hypothesis for the dispute surge, is still unverified (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION, OPEN).

If the rule change is later confirmed, a separate, unfinished step is required: billing engineering/ORG-UTIL must revert or patch the specific import validation rule misclassifying ACTUAL reads — this was not done in this release.

Dispute response time is confirmed within SLA (E-05: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA), so it is explicitly called out as not being a useful lever for reducing dispute volume, undercutting the original request's premise.
AMI handoff monitoring completeness is limited because the mdms-export tool is noted as DEGRADED, so AMI read-event visibility used to assess H-MDMS-BILL contribution may be incomplete.

This release does not remediate accounts that are already mis-billed; fixing those requires a separate manual rebill/credit review process under Billing Operations authority (K-BILLWRITE, via SR-MANUAL-REBILL-REVIEW-PROCESS), which was not executed here.

No automated bill writes or route-dispatch changes occurred in this release, in line with constraints K-BILLWRITE (bill writes require Billing Operations authority) and K-DISPATCH (route changes require Field Operations Manager confirmation, E-08).
